note: The source build compiles CPython's own dependency set rather than unpacking the prebuilt archives the upstream Android flow downloads. Versions and build numbers are the ones CPython 3.14.6 names, so this remains upstream's dependency set; only the two overrides below are applied.

recipes.single_revision_rationale: Every component is built from one recipe revision rather than from the tag that produced its published binary. Those tags are not contemporaneous: the older ones read the API level from a lowercase api_level variable that a caller setting ANDROID_API_LEVEL does not reach, and they pin different NDK revisions. Mixing them silently produced a dependency set at two different API levels. Since this build deliberately does not reproduce the published binaries — it changes the API level and OpenSSL's openssldir — matching each historical recipe matters less than the whole set being built the same way.

overrides.reason: the recipes pin the NDK one revision behind the one CPython pins; building the dependencies and the interpreter with different toolchains is a difference nobody chose

OpenSSL's default openssldir is /usr/local/ssl, which does not exist on Android, so the prebuilt archives ship a runtime with an unreachable trust store. This is the whole reason the dependencies are built from source rather than unpacked.

verification.versions_match_upstream: every version and build number here is the one CPython 3.14.6's Android/android.py unpack_deps names, so the source build produces the dependency set the interpreter expects
verification.recipe_downloads_are_unverified: the upstream recipes fetch their sources with wget and no checksum; the build pre-populates each recipe's download directory with the verified file above so the recipe finds it already present
verification.api_level_is_checked_per_object: the NDK stamps .note.android.ident into every executable and shared object; the build fails if any of them reports an API level other than the one requested
verification.compiler_is_checked: the recipe environment is evaluated once and the resolved CC must name the requested API level
